page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.2xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources comprise 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core and an overall 1:8 core-to-memory ratio.

Hardware expansion limits and peripheral configurations are structured around external network integration. The instance includes 0 local storage volumes, requiring external network-attached storage architectures such as Amazon EBS for persistent filesystem operations. In addition, the instance contains no GPU hardware accelerators and provides 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Host connectivity is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Relative to standard compute instances, the instance architecture trades dedicated local storage and graphical acceleration for an expanded memory footprint and a sustained 3.9 GHz processing frequency. This profile delivers cost efficiency for operations that require significant working memory allocations without justifying the physical overhead of specialized accelerators or local solid-state drives.

The r8ib.2xlarge configuration aligns with memory-heavy workloads including medium-scale in-memory databases, distributed memory caching nodes, enterprise relational databases, operational data analytics, and memory-bound batch processing.
